steps.title: Org shell, dashboard, settings, billing read-only
steps.goal: A church leader signs in and lands in their church at `/o/[orgSlug]/dashboard`, can switch between the churches they belong to, and — with `org.settings` — edits every `organization_settings` column the plan defines at `/o/[orgSlug]/settings` (sharing incl. share-link password rule and the founder's new `sermon_share_allow_download`, directory sharing flags, youth/adult ages with `youth_excludes_married` and `adult_groups_include_youth`, event flags, `push_on_bulletin`, timezone, logo upload to `org-assets`) and reads billing status at `/o/[orgSlug]/settings/billing`. Every org page and Server Action runs `requireOrgMember` + `requirePerm`; unknown/non-member slugs 404, missing permissions 403, `suspended` shows a banner and disables writes, `past_due` shows a banner only. The org sidebar exists with Dashboard/Settings/Billing; later steps add their entries. Build and lint/typecheck/test are green; users, sermons, announcements, bulletins are not touched.
steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 3.1 "Org shell, dashboard, settings, billing read-only" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §4 (`organization_settings`, "Key helper functions", "Client RPCs", "Permission mapping"), §5, §6 (`org-assets` bucket), §7 (`proxy.ts`, env vars) and §8, and `docs/DESIGN.md` §2 (the `apps/web` file list), §4.2 (`organizations`, `organization_settings` rows), §5 (mapping table, "Suspended orgs"), §6 (policy rows for `organizations`, `organization_settings`, `profiles`, `billing_*`, `audit_log`, and the storage-policies paragraph), §7 (bucket table), §9 and §11 Phase 1 step 7 before writing code. Also read `docs/RLS.md` (step 1.5) and `HANDOFF.md` "Deviations from plan" and "Decisions". Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
When you finish, a church leader can sign in, land in their church at `/o/[orgSlug]/dashboard`, switch between the churches they belong to, and — with `org.settings` — edit every organization setting the plan defines at `/o/[orgSlug]/settings` (sharing, the share-link password rule and the new allow-download rule, directory sharing flags, youth/adult ages with `youth_excludes_married` and `adult_groups_include_youth`, event flags, `push_on_bulletin`, timezone, logo upload to the `org-assets` bucket) and see a read-only billing page at `/o/[orgSlug]/settings/billing`. Every org page and Server Action is guarded by `requireOrgMember` + `requirePerm`, unknown or non-member slugs return 404, missing permissions return 403, a `suspended` church shows a banner and disables writes, and a `past_due` church shows a banner only. The org sidebar exists with entries for the pages built so far; steps 3.2–3.5 add theirs. `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` and `pnpm --filter web build` are green. Users, sermons, announcements, bulletins and share links are NOT part of this step.

## Inputs / prior state
- Step 2.1 created `apps/web` (package name `web`, Next 16.3, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui, RHF + `zodResolver`, TanStack Query, `sonner`), `apps/web/proxy.ts` (session refresh; unauthenticated `(super)`/`(org)` requests redirect to `/login?next=`), `src/lib/supabase/{server,client,service}.ts`, `src/lib/auth/{require-user,require-org,require-perm,require-super}.ts` (DESIGN §2 names; they wrap `my_context()` behind `React.cache`), `src/components/ui/*` and one theme token file (orchestrator decision 5). Read those files first: if `require-org.ts` already exports `requireOrgMember(slug)` and `require-perm.ts` exports `requirePerm(ctx, perm)`, extend them; if they are stubs, complete them with the signatures below.
- Step 2.2 created the super admin UI (`/admin/*`) including `src/features/orgs/SettingsForm.tsx` for the super admin's view of a church's settings. Do not reuse that component as-is for org admins; the org-side form in this step lives in `src/features/settings/` and may share a field-definition module with it (see Build 6).
- `9999_init.sql` (steps 1.2–1.4c) defines `organizations (id, slug citext unique, name, status org_status, billing_mode, trial_ends_at, contact_email)` and `organization_settings` with `timezone` (default `America/New_York`; trigger `app.validate_timezone` raises `invalid_timezone`, SQLSTATE 22023), `logo_path`, and the boolean/int columns listed in Build 4 (defaults per DESIGN §4.2; `sermon_share_allow_download` default false is founder decision 5). Check constraints: `youth_range` (`youth_min_age >= 5 and youth_min_age < youth_max_age and youth_max_age <= 40`), `adult_range` (`adult_min_age between youth_min_age and 21`), `fellowship_implies_congregation` (`(not directory_share_with_fellowship) or directory_share_in_congregation`). Policies: `organization_settings` select = member, update = `org.settings` ∧ `app.org_writable(org_id)`; `organizations` select = member or fellowship-visible; `billing_customers`/`billing_subscriptions`/`audit_log` select = `org.settings` or super; `profiles` update = own row. `org_status`: `trial, active, past_due, suspended, cancelled`; `app.org_writable` = status in (`trial`, `active`, `past_due`). `organization_settings` changes are audited by trigger — write no audit code.
- `my_context()` (step 1.3b) returns `{is_super_admin, orgs:[{org_id, slug, name, status, membership_status, person_id, household_id, permissions[]}], profile}`; `profiles.last_org_id` remembers the active church.
- Storage (1.4a, `docs/RLS.md`): bucket `org-assets` (private, 5 MiB, `image/jpeg`/`image/png`/`image/webp`, no SVG), path `{org_id}/logo/{uuid}.{ext}`; `ca_storage_insert` allows an upload only when `organization_settings.logo_path` already EQUALS the object name and the caller holds `org.settings`; no update/delete policy for `authenticated` — old objects are orphans swept by the 3.6 cron after 24 h. Reads use a 1 h signed URL from the user client.
- `@church/domain` (step 1.6): `PERMISSION_KEYS`, `PERMISSION_GROUPS`, `errors.ts` (maps `message` key + SQLSTATE from RPC/trigger errors), `dates.ts` (org timezone helpers), `schemas/org.ts` (or `schemas/settings.ts` — use whichever 1.6 created; if neither holds an organization-settings schema, add `organizationSettingsSchema` to `packages/domain/src/schemas/settings.ts` and export it from the package index). `@church/db` (step 1.7): `rpc.ts` (typed `myContext()` etc.), `queries/orgs.ts`, `queries/settings.ts`, `keys.ts`.
- Founder decisions that bind this step (quote them in code comments where they shape a field): decision 3 — "Each church sets its own youth age → `youth_min_age`, `youth_max_age`, `adult_min_age`, `youth_excludes_married`, `adult_groups_include_youth` editable in `/o/[slug]/settings` (defaults 13 / 25 / 18 / on / on). No schema change."; decision 5 — "DOWNLOADS ALLOWED when the church allows it → NEW column `organization_settings.sermon_share_allow_download boolean not null default false`"; decision 6 — "`push_on_bulletin` default true, per-church toggle"; decision 7 — "only `suspended` blocks writes; `past_due` = banner only"; decision 2 — fellowship viewers see "everything the congregation sees minus birth year, anniversary year, leader notes"; decision 1 — families may hide from their own congregation (that toggle is step 5.1; here only helper text).

## Build
1. **Guards** in `apps/web/src/lib/auth/`:
   - `require-org.ts`: `requireOrgMember(slug: string)` — `requireUser()` first (redirects to `/login?next=` when signed out), then `myContext()`; find `orgs` entry with `slug` (case-insensitive — `slug` is citext) and `membership_status = 'active'`. Not found, `pending`, or `disabled` → `notFound()` (a 404, so the URL does not reveal whether the church exists). Return `OrgContext = { org: {org_id, slug, name, status}, permissions: PermissionKey[], personId, householdId, isSuperAdmin, writable: status in ('trial','active','past_due') }`. Super admins who are not members also get 404 here — they use `/admin`; document this in a code comment (proposed change is listed in HANDOFF, not built).
   - `require-perm.ts`: `hasPerm(ctx, perm)`, `hasAnyPerm(ctx, perms[])`, and `requirePerm(ctx, perm | perms[])`, which calls Next's `forbidden()` when the actor lacks every listed permission. Set `experimental.authInterrupts: true` in `apps/web/next.config.ts`; add `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/forbidden.tsx` ("You do not have the <label> permission — ask a church administrator") and `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/not-found.tsx`. If `forbidden()` is unavailable in the installed Next 16.3, throw a `PermissionDeniedError` and render it from `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/error.tsx`; record which path you used in HANDOFF.
   - `requireWritable(ctx)` (in `require-org.ts`): throws `organization_suspended` (the same key the DB raises) when `ctx.writable` is false. Every mutating Server Action in this step calls it before touching the database, so the UI error matches the DB error (`app.require_writable`).
   - Server Actions never trust the client for the org: they receive `orgSlug`, re-run `requireOrgMember(orgSlug)` and `requirePerm`, validate with Zod, and write with the user client only (RLS enforces again). The service client (`src/lib/supabase/service.ts`) is NOT used anywhere in this step.
2. **Org route group**:
   - `app/(org)/o/page.tsx`: signed-in user with no slug → redirect to `/o/<slug>/dashboard` of `profile.last_org_id` when that org is in `orgs` with an active membership, else the first active org, else render a "You are not a member of any church yet" page (sign-out button; explain that an invitation link or a church administrator adds you; super admins get a link to `/admin`). Update step 2.1's post-login redirect so non-super users land on `/o` (leave super admins on `/admin`); if 2.1 already does this, keep it.
   - `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/page.tsx`: `redirect('/o/<slug>/dashboard')`.
   - `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/layout.tsx`: server component; `requireOrgMember(params.orgSlug)` (`params` is a Promise in Next 16 — `await` it); renders `src/features/org/OrgShell.tsx` (sidebar + top bar) with `src/features/org/OrgNav.tsx`, `src/features/org/OrgSwitcher.tsx`, `src/features/org/StatusBanner.tsx`, the church name and logo (signed URL, 1 h; TanStack caches 50 min — reuse the signed-URL helper if 2.x created one, else add `src/lib/storage/signed-url.ts` with `getSignedUrl(bucket, path, expiresIn = 3600)` using the user client). Provide `OrgContext` (minus nothing secret — it contains only what `my_context()` already returns to this user) to client components through a small React context `src/features/org/org-context.tsx`.
   - `OrgNav`: one config `src/features/org/nav.ts` exporting `NAV_ITEMS: {href, label, icon, requires?: PermissionKey[]}`; this step ships Dashboard (all members), Settings and Billing (`org.settings`) plus a commented placeholder list for later entries (3.2 Users/Invitations, 3.3 Sermons, 3.5 Announcements/Bulletins). Items the actor cannot access are hidden, not disabled; the active item follows the pathname.
   - `OrgSwitcher` (client): lists `orgs` with active membership; choosing one calls Server Action `switchOrg(slug)` in `src/features/org/actions.ts` which updates `profiles.last_org_id` (user client; own-row policy) and redirects to `/o/<slug>/dashboard`. Hidden when the user has one church. Super admins additionally see an "Super admin" link to `/admin`.
   - `StatusBanner`: `suspended` → red banner on every org page ("This church's account is suspended. Content is read-only until the super admin restores it.") and every form/button in this step disabled via `ctx.writable`; `past_due` → amber banner ("Payment is past due. Nothing is blocked yet — contact the super admin.", decision 7); `trial` → "Trial ends <date>" from `trial_ends_at` when not null; `cancelled` → verify `my_context()` omits such orgs (then the 404 applies); if it lists them, treat like suspended with a stronger message. Dates use the org timezone via `@church/domain/dates.ts`.
3. **Dashboard** `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/dashboard/page.tsx` + `src/features/org/Dashboard.tsx`: server-rendered cards using the user client (`@church/db/queries/*`; add small count helpers to `packages/db/src/queries/orgs.ts` if missing — keep them there, not in the app):
   - "Published sermons", "Active announcements", "Current bulletin" counts (`sermons`, `announcements`, `bulletins` with `publish_at <= now()`; RLS limits rows). Render the counts without links (no dead `#` links); steps 3.3/3.5 add the links (leave `TODO(3.3)`/`TODO(3.5)` comments).
   - "People with access" count of `org_memberships` where `status = 'active'` — only for holders of any `users.*` permission (others cannot read the rows; do not show 0).
   - A "Set up your church" checklist for new churches (`org.settings` holders only): logo uploaded (`logo_path` not null), timezone confirmed, sharing decided (`sermons_shareable`), directory sharing decided, ages reviewed, "invite your first users" (link to `/users` appears in 3.2). Each item links to the relevant settings section anchor (`/settings#sharing`, `#directory`, `#ages`, `#events`, `#notifications`, `#general`).
   - "Your permissions": the actor's permission labels under the three role headers from `PERMISSION_GROUPS` (`Sermon manager` / `Organization manager` / `Announcement manager` as step 1.5 recorded in HANDOFF), with the mapping tooltips from `@church/domain/permissions.ts` (decision 4: the DESIGN §5 mapping is the default).
4. **Settings page** `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/settings/page.tsx` (`requirePerm(ctx, 'org.settings')`), form `src/features/settings/SettingsForm.tsx` (client, RHF + `zodResolver`, one form, sections with ids used by the dashboard anchors), Server Actions in `src/features/settings/actions.ts`:
   - **General** (`#general`): church name (read-only here — `organizations` update is super admin only; show "ask the super admin to rename"), slug (read-only), `contact_email` (read-only), `timezone` — a searchable select fed by `Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone')` with the current value first; helper text "Ages, birthdays and 'today' are computed in this timezone"; the DB trigger rejects unknown names (`invalid_timezone`) — surface that message.
   - **Logo** (`#logo`): `src/features/settings/LogoUpload.tsx` — jpeg/png/webp ≤ 5 MiB (client check with a friendly message; the bucket enforces the same). Row-first flow because the insert policy demands it: (a) Server Action `prepareLogoUpload(orgSlug, ext)` computes `path = <org_id>/logo/<crypto.randomUUID()>.<ext>`, sets `organization_settings.logo_path = path` (user client) and returns `{path, previousPath}`; (b) the browser uploads with the user client `supabase.storage.from('org-assets').upload(path, file, { contentType: file.type, upsert: false })` (plain upload — TUS is for sermon media in 3.3); (c) success → `confirmLogoUpload(orgSlug, path)` re-checks the object via `storage.from('org-assets').list('<org_id>/logo')` and revalidates; (d) failure → `revertLogoUpload(orgSlug, previousPath)`. "Remove logo" sets `logo_path = null`; comment that the old object is swept by the 3.6 cron because `authenticated` has no delete policy. Preview via signed URL.
   - **Sharing** (`#sharing`): `sermons_shareable` ("Allow leaders to create public share links for sermons"), `sermon_share_requires_password` ("Share links must have a password (minimum 8 characters)"), `sermon_share_allow_download` ("Allow visitors to download uploaded sermon files from share links" — helper: external links (YouTube, Dropbox, Drive) always open at the provider; founder decision 5). Disable the two sub-toggles when `sermons_shareable` is off. Note in helper text that turning sharing off makes every existing share link return 404 immediately (DESIGN §7).
   - **Directory** (`#directory`): `directory_share_in_congregation` ("Members can see the church directory"), `directory_share_with_fellowship` ("Share the directory with churches in the same fellowship" — disabled and forced off when the congregation toggle is off, mirroring the `fellowship_implies_congregation` check; helper text quoting decision 2: fellowship churches see everything the congregation sees except birth years, anniversary years and leader notes), `fellowship_directory_adults_only` ("Only adults are visible to fellowship churches unless a family opts its children in"). Add a read-only note: "Families can hide themselves from the fellowship and from this congregation; leaders can only make a family more private" (decisions 1 and the direction rule) — the toggles themselves are step 5.1.
   - **Ages and groups** (`#ages`): `youth_min_age`, `youth_max_age`, `adult_min_age` (number inputs), `youth_excludes_married` ("Married people are not counted as youth"), `adult_groups_include_youth` ("Men's and Women's groups include youth"). Zod mirrors the DB checks with the same messages: 5 ≤ youth_min < youth_max ≤ 40; youth_min ≤ adult_min ≤ 21. Helper text: "Youth = ages <min>–<max>; adults = <adult_min>+; the head and spouse of a household are always adults; children are never in Men's or Women's" (DESIGN §4.3). Founder decision 3 in a comment.
   - **Events** (`#events`): `members_can_submit_events`, `events_require_approval` (helper: "Submissions by members without the announcements.create permission always start as pending"; the calendars/events UI is step 5.3).
   - **Notifications** (`#notifications`): `push_on_bulletin` ("Send a push notification when a bulletin is uploaded" — decision 6).
   - `saveSettings(orgSlug, input)`: `requireOrgMember` → `requirePerm('org.settings')` → `requireWritable` → Zod parse (`organizationSettingsSchema`) → `update organization_settings … where org_id = ctx.org.org_id` with the user client; map SQLSTATE `23514` (check violation) and `22023` (`invalid_timezone`) through `@church/domain/errors.ts` to field errors; `0 rows updated` means RLS refused (permission lost mid-session or org suspended) — show "You no longer have permission to change settings" and `revalidatePath`. `sonner` toast on success; Save disabled when `!ctx.writable`.
5. **Billing (read-only)** `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/settings/billing/page.tsx` + `src/features/settings/BillingStatus.tsx` (`requirePerm(ctx, 'org.settings')` — DESIGN §5 maps "view billing status" to `org.settings`): `organizations.status` badge, `billing_mode` (`stripe` / `manual` / `free`) with a one-line explanation each, `trial_ends_at` in the org timezone while `trial`, and, when `billing_mode = 'stripe'`, the latest `billing_subscriptions` row (`status`, `status_raw`, period end only if that column exists in `9999_init.sql`) read with the user client. Price text: "US$50 per month per church, billed by the super admin" (decision 7). No Checkout/Portal buttons — `/api/billing/checkout` and `/api/billing/portal` are super admin routes (2.3); say "Contact the super admin to change billing" (no email hard-coded). `past_due`/`suspended` explanations repeat the banner text.
6. **Shared field definitions**: put the label/helper/decision text for every settings field in `src/features/settings/fields.ts` so the super admin's `SettingsForm` (2.2) can import the same labels later; do not refactor 2.2's form now beyond importing labels if that is a one-line change.
7. **Queries and types**: add `getOrgBySlug`, `getSettings(orgId)`, `getBillingSummary(orgId)` and the dashboard counts to `packages/db/src/queries/{orgs,settings}.ts` (typed against `database.types.ts` — run `pnpm db:types` only if you changed nothing in SQL; you must not change SQL in this step). Add TanStack keys to `packages/db/src/keys.ts` for `settings`, `logoUrl`.
8. **Tests** (Vitest in `apps/web`, or `packages/domain` for the schema): `organizationSettingsSchema` accepts the defaults, rejects `youth_min_age = 30, youth_max_age = 25`, rejects `adult_min_age = 22`, rejects `directory_share_with_fellowship = true` with `directory_share_in_congregation = false`, rejects an unknown timezone; `nav.ts` visibility: no permissions → Dashboard only, `org.settings` → Settings and Billing; `hasAnyPerm` truth table. If 2.1 created `apps/web/e2e/smoke.spec.ts`, add: `/o/unknown-slug/dashboard` signed-out → redirect to `/login?next=…` (the signed-in flow is step 3.7).
9. **Docs**: `docs/RLS.md` gets a short "Web guards" subsection (how `requireOrgMember`/`requirePerm`/`requireWritable` map to `my_context()`, `app.has_perm`, `app.org_writable`); `docs/ENV.md` unchanged unless you add a variable (you should not need one).

## Constraints
- Do not edit `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` or add a migration; if a column or policy you need is missing, do the closest correct thing in the UI (hide the field) and record it in HANDOFF "Deviations from plan" — do not change SQL in a web step. Never run `supabase db push` or `db reset`.
- Web never holds elevated keys: the service client is not imported by any file in this step. All reads/writes go through the user-scoped server client under RLS; no `srv_*` RPC is called here.
- `organizations` (name, slug, status, billing_mode, trial_ends_at) is super-admin-owned: the org side never updates it.
- Keep 2.1/2.2 code intact except the guard files, the post-login redirect and the optional label import; no refactors of `/admin`, no Stripe code, no push code, no `/users`, `/sermons`, `/announcements`, `/bulletins` pages (those are 3.2–3.5; the nav config carries commented placeholders only).
- Next 16: `params`/`searchParams` are Promises; `cookies()` is async; Server Actions live in `'use server'` files; `revalidatePath` after writes. Keep 2.1's `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and CSP; the logo preview is an `<img>` with a signed URL (add the Supabase host to `img-src` if 2.1 did not).
- Versions: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3 exact, `@supabase/ssr` 0.12, supabase-js 2.112, Zod 4.5, TypeScript ~5.9 (not 7), ESLint 9 (not 10), Tailwind 4, Vitest 4. No new runtime dependency except shadcn components generated into `src/components/ui/*` (`command` for the timezone select, `switch`, `tooltip`, `alert`).
- Permission labels and tooltips come from `@church/domain/permissions.ts`; never hard-code the 12 keys in the app.
- No email addresses, keys or model names in code, comments, or commits. Use `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` placeholders only in docs if you must mention one.
- Do not build the org-side `hide_from_congregation`/directory toggles (5.1), the users grid (3.2) or super-admin membership access to org pages.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → every task succeeds; the new Vitest cases pass (schema refinements, nav visibility, `hasAnyPerm`).
- `pnpm --filter web build` → succeeds; the route list printed by Next includes `/o`, `/o/[orgSlug]`, `/o/[orgSlug]/dashboard`, `/o/[orgSlug]/settings`, `/o/[orgSlug]/settings/billing` and no build-time data fetching (all dynamic).
- Local DB run (no SQL changed): `scripts/db/local-up.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh && scripts/db/test.sh` → all green, unchanged. The web app cannot sign in against the local shim (no GoTrue), so the manual check runs against the hosted project once 2.4/2.5 are done; otherwise record it as pending in HANDOFF.
- Manual check against the hosted project (record as pending if `apps/web/.env.local` has no hosted values): sign in as the first church admin from 2.5 → `/o` redirects to `/o/<slug>/dashboard`; `/o/does-not-exist/dashboard` → 404; remove `org.settings` from that admin in `/admin/churches/[orgId]` → `/o/<slug>/settings` → 403 and Settings hidden from the nav; restore it; `youth_max_age` 24 → saved with toast; `youth_max_age` 3 → inline error, nothing saved; `directory_share_with_fellowship` while congregation sharing is off → toggle disabled (forced via devtools → DB check error as a field error); upload a 200 KB PNG logo → visible in the sidebar after one reload; set the church `suspended` in `/admin` → banner everywhere, Save disabled, `saveSettings` refused; set it back to `active`.
- `git grep -n "service" apps/web/app/\(org\) apps/web/src/features/org apps/web/src/features/settings` → no import of `src/lib/supabase/service`.
- `git grep -n "sermon_share_allow_download" apps/web packages` → the toggle, its label and the Zod schema all reference the column.

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: tick "Web: … org admin (settings)" progress in the State checklist (keep users/permissions unticked), set the feature-table row "Org admin settings (sharing, share-link password)" Web UI to "done (3.1; allow-download toggle included)", record which 403 mechanism you used (`forbidden()` vs `error.tsx`), the `/o` landing behaviour, the note that super admins are not org members (404 on `/o/<slug>` unless invited), and any deviation under "Deviations from plan".
- Tick step 3.1 in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat(web): org shell, dashboard, settings, read-only billing`; push `main` (`git push origin main`) unless another branch was named.
- If anything in the plan proves impossible or wrong (for example a settings column that does not exist in `9999_init.sql`, or `forbidden()` unavailable), do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.
done_when: `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` and `pnpm --filter web build` succeed; the build lists routes `/o`, `/o/[orgSlug]`, `/o/[orgSlug]/dashboard`, `/o/[orgSlug]/settings`, `/o/[orgSlug]/settings/billing`, and `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/{layout,not-found,forbidden or error}.tsx` exist.

`apps/web/src/lib/auth/require-org.ts` exports `requireOrgMember(slug)` (404 for unknown slug, non-member, pending or disabled membership) and `requireWritable`; `require-perm.ts` exports `hasPerm`, `hasAnyPerm`, `requirePerm` (403); every page and Server Action under `app/(org)` and `src/features/{org,settings}` calls them, and none imports `src/lib/supabase/service`.

`/o/[orgSlug]/settings` (org.settings only) edits timezone, logo, `sermons_shareable`, `sermon_share_requires_password`, `sermon_share_allow_download`, `directory_share_in_congregation`, `directory_share_with_fellowship`, `fellowship_directory_adults_only`, `youth_min_age`, `youth_max_age`, `adult_min_age`, `youth_excludes_married`, `adult_groups_include_youth`, `members_can_submit_events`, `events_require_approval`, `push_on_bulletin`; the Zod schema mirrors the three DB checks and Vitest proves the rejections; DB errors 23514/22023 surface as field errors.

Logo upload follows row-first flow (`prepareLogoUpload` sets `logo_path` to `<org_id>/logo/<uuid>.<ext>` → browser upload to `org-assets` with the user client → confirm/revert), rejects files over 5 MiB or outside jpeg/png/webp, and the sidebar shows the logo through a 1 h signed URL.

`/o/[orgSlug]/settings/billing` (org.settings only) shows status badge, `billing_mode`, `trial_ends_at` in the org timezone, the latest `billing_subscriptions` row when `billing_mode = 'stripe'`, the US$50/month text, and no Stripe buttons.

Status banners: `suspended` → red banner on every org page with all write controls disabled and `saveSettings` refusing with `organization_suspended`; `past_due` → amber banner only; `trial` → trial-end line; `OrgSwitcher` updates `profiles.last_org_id` and `/o` redirects to that church (or the first active one, or a no-church page).

Dashboard shows permission-aware counts (published sermons, active announcements, current bulletin; membership count only for `users.*` holders), a set-up checklist for `org.settings` holders linking to settings section anchors, and the actor's permissions grouped under the three role headers with mapping tooltips from `@church/domain`.
`src/features/org/nav.ts` is the single nav config (Dashboard, Settings, Billing, commented placeholders for 3.2–3.5) and items are hidden, not disabled, when the actor lacks the permission.

HANDOFF.md records the 403 mechanism, the `/o` landing rule, the super-admin-not-a-member note and any deviation; feature-table row for org admin settings is marked done; docs/TODO.md step 3.1 is ticked; `session_log.md` written; commit `feat(web): org shell, dashboard, settings, read-only billing` pushed.

steps.title: Users & permissions
steps.goal: A church leader with any `users.*` permission manages access at `/o/[orgSlug]/users`: a grid of memberships × the 12 permission checkboxes under the three role headers with per-header select-all, debounced optimistic saves via `set_membership_permissions`, and checkboxes disabled with a tooltip without `users.edit_permissions`. `users.create` holders invite by email (`create_invitation`; Resend when `RESEND_API_KEY`/`RESEND_FROM` are set, else the `/invite/[token]` link shown once) or create accounts directly (`createUserDirect` → `auth.admin.createUser` → `srv_attach_user`, temporary password shown once, linked to an existing directory person or a new one-person household). `users.delete` holders disable/remove; re-enable/approve needs `users.create`; the last-manager guard error is readable. `/users/[membershipId]` and `/invitations` (revoke, resend) exist; the service client is used only inside `src/lib/users/create-direct.ts`.
steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 3.2 "Users & permissions" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §4 (tables `profiles`, `org_memberships`, `org_membership_permissions`, `invitations`; "Client RPCs", "Server-only RPCs", "Permission mapping for unnamed capabilities"), §5, §7 (rows "Direct user creation", "Invitations", env list) and §8, and `docs/DESIGN.md` §2 (`apps/web` file list), §3 (`resend` pin), §4.2 (the same tables plus `persons`), §4.4 "RPC semantics", §5 (mapping table, "Getting accounts" paths 1–3), §6 (policy rows for those tables), §8, §9 (permission-grid paragraph) and §11 Phase 1 step 7 before writing code. Also read `docs/RLS.md` (mapping, error catalogue) and `HANDOFF.md` ("Deviations from plan", "Decisions"). Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
When you finish, a church leader with any `users.*` permission opens `/o/[orgSlug]/users` and sees every membership as a grid: one row per user, twelve checkboxes under the three role headers (Sermon manager / Organization manager / Announcement manager), select-all per header, debounced optimistic saves through `set_membership_permissions`, and checkboxes disabled with a tooltip when the actor lacks `users.edit_permissions`. Holders of `users.create` invite by email (`create_invitation`; emailed through Resend when configured, otherwise the link is shown once) or create an account directly (`createUserDirect`: temporary password shown once, linked to an existing directory person or a new one-person household). Holders of `users.delete` disable and remove memberships (re-enable needs `users.create`); the last-manager guard error reads clearly. `/o/[orgSlug]/users/[membershipId]` shows one membership; `/o/[orgSlug]/invitations` lists pending invitations with revoke and resend. Lint/typecheck/test and the web build are green. The directory UI (households, persons, privacy) is NOT part of this step — only the minimal person picker the dialogs need.

## Inputs / prior state
- Step 3.1 created the org shell: `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/layout.tsx`, `src/lib/auth/require-org.ts` (`requireOrgMember(slug)` → `OrgContext { org, permissions, personId, householdId, isSuperAdmin, writable }`, `requireWritable(ctx)`), `src/lib/auth/require-perm.ts` (`hasPerm`, `hasAnyPerm`, `requirePerm` → 403), `src/features/org/nav.ts` (`NAV_ITEMS` with commented placeholders for Users and Invitations), `src/features/org/org-context.tsx`, `StatusBanner`, the dashboard's "invite your first users" checklist item (currently without a link) and `src/lib/storage/signed-url.ts`. Read those files first and reuse them; do not duplicate guards.
- Step 2.1 created `src/lib/supabase/{server,client,service}.ts` (the service client reads `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY ?? SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` and is server-only), `app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx` (accepts an invitation via `accept_invitation(token)` and offers "Open in app"), `src/components/ui/*` (shadcn: button, input, card, dialog, checkbox, table, tabs, select, badge, toast/sonner; 3.1 added switch, tooltip, alert, command).
- Step 2.2 created `/admin/churches/[orgId]` with an Admins tab that invites or creates the first admin with all 12 permissions; it already contains a first version of the direct-creation flow (look for `createUserDirect` or an equivalent in `src/features/orgs/` or `src/lib/users/`). If 2.2 built `src/lib/users/create-direct.ts`, extend it; if it inlined the logic, move it into `src/lib/users/create-direct.ts` in this step and make the Admins tab import it (that is the only permitted change to `/admin`).
- `9999_init.sql` (steps 1.2–1.4c) defines `profiles (user_id, display_name, email citext, last_org_id)`, `org_memberships (id, org_id, user_id, status membership_status, invited_by, approved_by, approved_at, disabled_at)` unique `(org_id, user_id)`, `org_membership_permissions (membership_id, permission, granted_by, granted_at)`, `invitations (id, org_id, email, person_id null, permissions permission_key[], invited_by, expires_at default now()+14d, accepted_at, accepted_by, revoked_at)` (token hash in `private.invitation_secrets`), and `persons.user_id` (partial unique per org). Trigger `app.guard_last_org_manager` blocks removing the last active `users.edit_permissions` holder and raises the message key 1.3b catalogued (`last_org_manager` in the G2 draft — read `docs/RLS.md` for the exact key and SQLSTATE). All four tables are audited by trigger; write no audit code.
- Policies (DESIGN §6): `profiles` select = own row or `users.*` holder of a shared org, update = own row; `org_memberships` and `org_membership_permissions` select = own row or any `users.*` permission, writes RPC-only; `invitations` select = `users.create`, writes RPC-only; `persons`/`households` select through the `directory_persons` / `directory_households` views only (directory admins = `users.create` or `org.settings` see every listed person). There are no insert/update/delete grants on these tables for `authenticated` — every write in this step is an RPC call.
- RPCs (PLAN §4, DESIGN §4.4): `set_membership_permissions(membership_id, perms[])` — `users.edit_permissions`, org derived from the row, last-manager guard, audits the diff; `set_membership_status(id, status)` — `disabled` needs `users.delete`, `active` needs `users.create`; `remove_membership(id)` — `users.delete`; hard-deletes membership + permissions, nulls `persons.user_id`, deletes that user's `push_devices` / `notification_preferences` for the org; `create_invitation(org, email, person_id, perms[])` — `users.create`, **non-empty `perms` requires `users.edit_permissions`**, returns the raw token once; `revoke_invitation(id)`; `accept_invitation(token)` is used by the 2.1 invite page, not here. Server-only: `srv_attach_user(user_id, org_id, person_id, display_name, perms[])` — active membership + person link or creation. Every mutating RPC calls `app.require_writable(org)` — a suspended church rejects them with `organization_suspended`.
- `@church/domain` (step 1.6): `PERMISSION_KEYS` (12-tuple in enum order), `PERMISSION_GROUPS` (three headers), labels/tooltips with the mapping text, `errors.ts` (maps RPC errors by message key + SQLSTATE), `schemas/*` (read `packages/domain/src/schemas/` and extend rather than duplicate). `@church/db` (step 1.7): `rpc.ts` typed wrappers for every RPC above including `srvAttachUser`, `queries/*`, `keys.ts`.
- Founder decisions that bind this step: decision 4 — "Permission mapping (docs/DESIGN.md §5 table) ships as the default — document it" (grid tooltips repeat that text); decision 7 — "only `suspended` blocks writes; `past_due` = banner only"; PLAN §4 mapping — "invite/create accounts = `users.create` (granting perms also needs `users.edit_permissions`); remove access = `users.delete`; directory admin = `users.create` or `org.settings`"; DESIGN §5 — "one auth account may be shared by a household (linked to one person only)". Env (PLAN §7): `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM` (optional), `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`.

## Build
1. **Queries** in `packages/db/src/queries/users.ts` (new; keep them in the package, typed against `database.types.ts`, no SQL changes): `listMemberships(orgId)` — `org_memberships` joined to `profiles` (`display_name`, `email`), `org_membership_permissions` and the linked `directory_persons` row (`first_name`, `last_name`, `household_id`), ordered by status (`active`, `pending`, `disabled`) then name; `getMembership(membershipId)`; `listInvitations(orgId)` — rows with `accepted_at is null and revoked_at is null`, newest first, `expires_at < now()` flagged; `listLinkablePersons(orgId, search)` — `directory_persons` with `user_id is null` and `deceased_on is null`, `ilike` name search, limit 20. Add keys to `packages/db/src/keys.ts` (`memberships`, `invitations`, `linkablePersons`). No directory mutation queries — 5.1 owns them.
2. **Nav and dashboard**: uncomment/add in `src/features/org/nav.ts` the entries `Users` (`/o/[orgSlug]/users`, `requires: ['users.create','users.delete','users.edit_permissions']` — any of them) and `Invitations` (`/o/[orgSlug]/invitations`, `requires: ['users.create']`). Give the 3.1 dashboard checklist item "invite your first users" its link to `/o/[orgSlug]/users` (visible to `users.create` holders) and show the "People with access" count as a link to `/users` for `users.*` holders.
3. **Users page** `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/users/page.tsx`: `requireOrgMember` then `requirePerm(ctx, ['users.create','users.delete','users.edit_permissions'])` (any). Server component loads `listMemberships` with the user client and renders `src/features/users/UsersPage.tsx` (client shell): toolbar with "Invite" (`users.create`), "Create account" (`users.create`), search box (name/email, client-side), status filter (Active / Pending / Disabled / All; default Active + Pending), and `src/features/users/PermissionGrid.tsx`.
4. **PermissionGrid** (`src/features/users/PermissionGrid.tsx`, client):
   - Rows = memberships; first column = display name (link to `/users/[membershipId]`), email, linked person name or "Not linked to a directory person", status badge (`pending` amber, `disabled` grey; `disabled` rows render their checkboxes disabled with the tooltip "Re-enable this user to change permissions"). "(you)" marker on the actor's own row.
   - Columns = the 12 permissions in `PERMISSION_KEYS` order, grouped under the three headers from `PERMISSION_GROUPS` (Sermon manager / Organization manager / Announcement manager, labels from `@church/domain`; never hard-code the keys). Each row has a select-all checkbox under each header (checked when the row holds every key of the group, indeterminate when some) that toggles that whole group for that row — PLAN §8's "role-header select-all"; a column-wide select-all across users is not required. Header cells and checkboxes carry tooltips: the label plus the mapping text from `@church/domain/permissions.ts` (e.g. `users.create` → directory admin + invite/create accounts; `org.settings` → directory admin, settings, billing status, audit, calendars, custom groups; `users.delete` → disable/remove access; `sermons.link`/`sermons.upload` → share links; `announcements.*` → surveys, custom groups, event approval).
   - Without `users.edit_permissions` every checkbox is disabled and the tooltip reads "You need the users.edit_permissions permission to change permissions" (DESIGN §9). A `suspended` church (`!ctx.writable`) disables everything with the 3.1 banner text.
   - Editing model: keep local state per row (`Set<PermissionKey>`); a change updates the UI immediately (optimistic), then a per-row debounce (400 ms, `src/features/users/use-debounced-permissions.ts`) calls the Server Action `updatePermissions(orgSlug, membershipId, perms[])` with the **full** set (the RPC takes the whole array, not a diff). On error revert that row to the last server-confirmed set and toast the mapped message; on success replace the confirmed set. Coalesce: a change arriving while a save is in flight saves again after it resolves (one in-flight request per row). Unticking your own `users.edit_permissions` asks for confirmation first; the DB last-manager guard is the real protection — map its key to "This is the last user who can manage permissions; grant users.edit_permissions to someone else first".
   - Put the pure logic (toggle key, toggle group, group state all/some/none, set equality, coalescing state machine) in `src/features/users/permission-grid.logic.ts` and unit-test it.
5. **Server Actions** in `src/features/users/actions.ts` (`'use server'`; every action: `requireOrgMember(orgSlug)` → `requirePerm` → `requireWritable(ctx)` → Zod parse → RPC via `@church/db/rpc` with the **user** client → `revalidatePath('/o/<slug>/users')` → return `{ ok } | { ok: false, error }` with the message mapped by `@church/domain/errors.ts`):
   - `updatePermissions(orgSlug, membershipId, perms)` — `users.edit_permissions`; calls `set_membership_permissions`.
   - `setMembershipStatus(orgSlug, membershipId, status)` — `'disabled'` requires `users.delete`, `'active'` requires `users.create` (approving a `pending` row or re-enabling); calls `set_membership_status`.
   - `removeMembership(orgSlug, membershipId)` — `users.delete`; calls `remove_membership`.
   - `inviteUser(orgSlug, input)` — `users.create`; if `input.permissions.length > 0` also `requirePerm(ctx, 'users.edit_permissions')` (mirror the RPC rule so the UI error is immediate); calls `create_invitation(org_id, email, person_id ?? null, perms)`; builds `link = ${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}/invite/${token}`; calls `sendInvitationEmail` (Build 8); returns `{ ok, invitationId, link, emailed: boolean }`. The raw token is returned to the browser exactly once and never logged or stored (the DB keeps only the hash).
   - `revokeInvitation(orgSlug, invitationId)` — `users.create`; calls `revoke_invitation`.
   - `resendInvitation(orgSlug, invitationId)` — `users.create`; the raw token exists only at creation, so resend = `revoke_invitation(old)` then `create_invitation` with the same `email`, `person_id`, `permissions` (with `[]` and a toast note if the actor no longer holds `users.edit_permissions`), then email or return the new link.
   - `createAccount(orgSlug, input)` — `users.create` (+ `users.edit_permissions` when permissions are non-empty); delegates to `src/lib/users/create-direct.ts` (Build 7). All other actions never import the service client.
6. **Dialogs**:
   - `src/features/users/InviteDialog.tsx` (RHF + `zodResolver`, schema from `@church/domain`): email (required, citext-normalised to lowercase in the schema), optional directory person (`src/features/users/PersonPicker.tsx` — a `command`-based searchable list fed by `listLinkablePersons` through TanStack Query; shows "first last · household" and "Create a new person for them" as the default), permissions (the same 12-checkbox block with headers, reused from a `src/features/users/PermissionPicker.tsx` component shared with the grid; hidden with the note "You need users.edit_permissions to invite with permissions" when the actor lacks it). On success: if `emailed` → "Invitation sent to <email>. It expires in 14 days."; else show the link in a read-only input with a Copy button and "This link is shown once. Copy it now and send it yourself." Note that the recipient must sign up or sign in with the same email (`accept_invitation` verifies it) and that existing accounts simply gain the church/permissions.
   - `src/features/users/CreateAccountDialog.tsx`: email (required), display name (required; prefilled from the picked person), person: "Link to an existing directory person" (PersonPicker, persons without `user_id` only) or "Create a new one-person household" (first name, last name required), permissions (as above), and a temporary password generated in the browser by `src/lib/users/temp-password.ts` (16 characters, `crypto.getRandomValues`, unambiguous alphabet, regenerate button; editable). On success show the email + temporary password **once** with Copy buttons: "Give these to the person in private. They sign in at <app url>/login and should change the password." Helper text: "One account may be shared by a household, but it is linked to one directory person only." Both dialog buttons are hidden when `!ctx.writable`.
7. **Direct creation** `src/lib/users/create-direct.ts` — `createUserDirect(ctx, input: { email, tempPassword, displayName, personId | newPerson: {firstName, lastName}, permissions })` (server-only module; the ONLY file in this step that imports `src/lib/supabase/service.ts`): (a) re-verify with the user client that `ctx` holds `users.create` (and `users.edit_permissions` if `permissions.length > 0`, else pass `[]`) and `ctx.writable`; (b) `service.auth.admin.createUser({ email, password: tempPassword, email_confirm: true, user_metadata: { display_name } })`; if the email already exists, find the user with `service.auth.admin.listUsers` (or `getUserByEmail` if supabase-js 2.112 exposes it), continue with that `user_id` WITHOUT changing its password, and return `existingAccount: true` so the dialog says "This email already had an account; we added them to your church. Their existing password still applies."; (c) `srv_attach_user(user_id, org_id, person_id ?? null, display_name, perms)` with the service client — for a null `personId` pass `display_name = "<first> <last>"` and let the RPC create the one-person household + person (read `9999_init.sql` to confirm its null-`person_id` behaviour; adapt the call, never the SQL); (d) if `srv_attach_user` fails after a **new** auth user was created, `auth.admin.deleteUser` it so no orphan account remains, then rethrow; (e) return `{ userId, membershipId, existingAccount }`. The temporary password is never logged or stored server-side.
8. **Email** `src/lib/email/resend.ts`: `isEmailConfigured()` = both `RESEND_API_KEY` and `RESEND_FROM` set; `sendInvitationEmail({ to, orgName, inviterName, link, expiresAt })` uses `resend` 6.25.0 (DESIGN §3; the only new runtime dependency) with a plain-text + minimal HTML body: church name, inviter, the https link, the expiry, "If you did not expect this, ignore it." Returns `{ sent: true } | { sent: false, reason: 'not_configured' | 'error', message }`; on `error` the Server Action still returns the link for copy/paste (the invitation exists either way). Never send from the browser; the token appears only inside the link.
9. **Membership actions** `src/features/users/MembershipActions.tsx`: dropdown per row and on the detail page — "Disable access" (`users.delete`; confirm "They keep their account but lose access to this church; you can re-enable them"), "Re-enable" and "Approve" for `pending` rows (`users.create`; `set_membership_status(id, 'active')`), "Remove from church" (`users.delete`; destructive confirm listing the RPC's consequences: membership and permissions deleted, directory person unlinked but kept, push devices for this church removed). Hide items the actor cannot perform and Disable/Remove on the actor's own row (no self-removal — leave a comment). Surface the last-manager error and `organization_suspended` as toasts with the mapped messages.
10. **Detail page** `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/users/[membershipId]/page.tsx` (`params` is a Promise): same permission rule as the list; `getMembership` with the user client — 404 when the row is not visible (RLS returns nothing). Sections: profile (display name, email), status with `approved_at` / `disabled_at` / `invited_by` name, linked directory person ("Not linked" — linking moves to the directory in step 5.1; no picker here), permissions (`PermissionPicker` bound to `updatePermissions`, same disabled rules), `MembershipActions`, and for `org.settings` holders the last 20 `audit_log` rows for this membership (filter by row id; skip the section if `9999_init.sql`'s columns make that awkward and note it in HANDOFF).
11. **Invitations page** `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/invitations/page.tsx` (`requirePerm(ctx, 'users.create')`) + `src/features/users/InvitationsTable.tsx`: email, linked person, permission count with a tooltip listing them, invited by, created, expires (red "Expired" when past — the 3.6 cron's `srv_housekeeping` prunes them later), actions Resend and Revoke (Build 5), and the same `InviteDialog` behind an "Invite" button. Accepted and revoked invitations are not listed (they remain in the audit log).
12. **Domain**: extend `packages/domain/src/schemas/` with `inviteUserSchema` (`email` (trim, lowercase, max 254), `personId` uuid nullable, `permissions` array of `PERMISSION_KEYS` default `[]`) and `createAccountSchema` (`email`, `displayName` 1–80, `tempPassword` 12–72 chars, `personId` xor `newPerson`, `permissions`), exported from the package index; reuse 1.6's names if they already exist. Add unit tests for both (valid, missing email, both `personId` and `newPerson`, unknown permission key).
13. **Tests** (Vitest): `permission-grid.logic.ts` (toggle key, group all/some/none, select-all touches only its group, equality, coalesced save state), `temp-password.ts` (length, alphabet, randomness), `resend.ts` with env unset → `{ sent: false, reason: 'not_configured' }` (lazy-import the SDK so the build needs no key), and the two schemas. If `apps/web/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` exists, add signed-out `/o/some-church/users` and `/o/some-church/invitations` → redirect to `/login?next=…`.
14. **Docs**: `docs/RLS.md` "Web guards" subsection (3.1) gets the users rules: which permission each action needs, the invite-with-permissions rule, the last-manager guard behaviour, and the direct-creation path (service client only inside `create-direct.ts`). `docs/ENV.md`: `RESEND_API_KEY` / `RESEND_FROM` marked optional with the copy-link fallback described.

## Constraints
- Do not edit `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` and do not add a migration; if an RPC signature differs from the docs, call it as it is in the SQL and note the difference in HANDOFF "Deviations from plan". Never run `supabase db push` or `db reset`.
- Web never holds elevated keys: `src/lib/supabase/service.ts` is imported by `src/lib/users/create-direct.ts` only (plus 2.x files that already used it); `srv_attach_user` is the only `srv_*` RPC called. Everything else uses the user-scoped server client under RLS and the `public.*` RPCs — no direct table writes on `org_memberships`, `org_membership_permissions`, `invitations`, `persons` or `households`.
- The grid sends the full permission array; never compute diffs client-side for the RPC. Never hard-code the 12 keys or the three headers: import `PERMISSION_KEYS`, `PERMISSION_GROUPS` and labels from `@church/domain`.
- Raw invitation tokens and temporary passwords appear once in the Server Action response and the dialog; never in logs, `console.*`, URLs of the admin UI, the database, `sessionStorage`, or toasts that persist.
- Directory data is read only through `directory_persons` / `directory_households`; no person/household editing UI (step 5.1). No join codes or join requests (5.6). No `/admin` changes beyond importing `create-direct.ts`.
- Next 16: `params`/`searchParams` are Promises; Server Actions in `'use server'` files; `revalidatePath` after writes; keep 2.1's CSP and headers. Versions: Next 16.3, React 19.2.3 exact, `@supabase/ssr` 0.12, supabase-js 2.112, Zod 4.5, TypeScript ~5.9 (not 7), ESLint 9 (not 10), Tailwind 4, Vitest 4, `resend` 6.25.0 (the only new runtime dependency; shadcn components generated into `src/components/ui/*` as needed: `dropdown-menu`, `popover`, `command`, `alert-dialog`).
- No email addresses, keys or model names in code, comments, tests or commits; test fixtures use `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`-style placeholders or `example.com` addresses only.

## Verify

## Finish

Add `RESEND_API_KEY` / `RESEND_FROM` to the founder to-dos as optional (step 3.9 covers them).
- Tick step 3.2 in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat(web): users grid, invitations, direct accounts`; push `main` (`git push origin main`) unless another branch was named.
- If anything in the plan proves impossible or wrong (for example `srv_attach_user` not creating a person for a null `person_id`, or `auth.admin.createUser` behaving differently in supabase-js 2.112), do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.

steps.notes: Depends on 3.1 (guards, nav, org context) and transitively on 2.1 (invite page, service client), 2.2 (first direct-create code), 1.6/1.7. Names chosen where the docs are silent: `packages/db/src/queries/users.ts` with `listMemberships`/`getMembership`/`listInvitations`/`listLinkablePersons`; Server Actions `updatePermissions`, `setMembershipStatus`, `removeMembership`, `inviteUser`, `revokeInvitation`, `resendInvitation`, `createAccount`; components `UsersPage`, `PersonPicker`, `PermissionPicker`, `InvitationsTable`, `permission-grid.logic.ts`, `use-debounced-permissions.ts`; `src/lib/users/temp-password.ts`; schemas `inviteUserSchema` / `createAccountSchema`; email helper `isEmailConfigured` / `sendInvitationEmail`. Resend of an invitation is revoke + create because the raw token is returned only at creation (DESIGN §4.4). Direct creation for an email that already has an auth account attaches the existing user without touching its password (DESIGN §5 shared-household accounts); the prompt makes the agent verify how `srv_attach_user` handles a null `person_id` (docs say 'person link/creation') and adapt the call, never the SQL. The service client is confined to `create-direct.ts`. Linking a membership to a different person is deferred to 5.1 (directory admin). Manual hosted check is recorded as pending if 2.4/2.5 are not yet done. No split: about 20 new files, one new runtime dependency (`resend` 6.25.0).

open_issues: Super admins are not org members (DESIGN §5: super admin is a `super_admins` row, never a membership), so the founder trialling as super admin gets 404 on `/o/<slug>/*` unless he invites himself into the church (2.2 Admins tab → create/invite with all 12 permissions). 3.1 documents this; the orchestrator may want 2.5's checklist to tell the founder to add himself as the first church admin, or a later step to let super admins open org pages read-only.

Guard file names/signatures are chosen by G5 (2.1) in parallel: 3.1 assumes DESIGN §2's `src/lib/auth/{require-user,require-org,require-perm,require-super}.ts` with `requireOrgMember(slug)` / `requirePerm(ctx, perm)` (PLAN §8 names) and tells the agent to extend whatever exists. If G5 chose different names, the assembler should align 3.1 (and 3.2–3.5) to them.

Post-login landing for non-super users (`/o` → last_org_id) is placed in 3.1; if G5's 2.1 already redirects members somewhere else, 3.1 keeps 2.1's behaviour only when it lands on `/o` or `/o/<slug>/dashboard`.

403 handling relies on Next's `forbidden()` + `experimental.authInterrupts` (Next 15.1+; assumed still experimental in 16.3). The prompt gives an `error.tsx` fallback; G10 (3.7 Playwright) should assert whichever mechanism HANDOFF records.

Settings Zod schema location: the skeleton lists `schemas/*` (org, settings, …) for 1.6 but G4 is drafted in parallel; 3.1 uses `organizationSettingsSchema` from `@church/domain` and creates `schemas/settings.ts` only if 1.6 did not. G4 should export a schema by that name (or the assembler renames one side).

Logo replacement orphans: `org-assets` has no delete policy for `authenticated` (DESIGN §6), so old logos are removed only by the 3.6 cron orphan sweep (> 24 h). If the orchestrator prefers immediate cleanup, 3.1 would need a service-client Server Action inserting into `storage_deletions`, which the skeleton reserves for cron/service paths — not built here.

`billing_subscriptions` column names beyond `status`/`status_raw`/`event_created` (e.g. current period end) were fixed by G2 (1.2); 3.1 tells the agent to read `9999_init.sql` rather than assume. G6 (2.3) chose the Stripe sync columns — 3.1's billing page shows only what exists.

[3.2] `srv_attach_user(user_id, org_id, person_id, display_name, perms[])` is documented as 'person link/creation' but the docs do not say what it creates for a null `person_id` (one-person household with `created_via='admin'`? first/last name split from `display_name`?). G2 (1.3b) fixed the body; 3.2 tells the agent to read the SQL and adapt the call. The assembler should align 3.2's `createUserDirect` input (`newPerson: {firstName, lastName}`) with what 1.3b actually implemented.

[3.2] Direct creation for an email that already has an auth account: DESIGN §5 allows one shared household account, so 3.2 attaches the existing user (no password change) via `srv_attach_user`. supabase-js 2.112 `auth.admin` may or may not expose `getUserByEmail`; the prompt falls back to `listUsers`. If the orchestrator prefers to refuse existing emails instead, drop that branch.

[3.2] Resending an invitation is implemented as revoke + new `create_invitation` (new token) because the raw token is only returned once; a dedicated `resend_invitation` RPC would need a migration and is not proposed.
[3.2] The last-manager error message key is `last_org_manager` in G2's draft of 1.3b; 3.2 tells the agent to read `docs/RLS.md` for the exact key. The assembler should make 1.5's docs/RLS.md list it.

[3.2] `pending` memberships exist in the enum but Phase 1 creates none (invitations accept straight to `active`; join requests are 5.6). 3.2 still renders and approves them so 5.6 needs no grid change.

[3.2] Names chosen for files/actions not in the docs (`queries/users.ts`, `PersonPicker`, `PermissionPicker`, `InvitationsTable`, `temp-password.ts`, `inviteUserSchema`, `createAccountSchema`); G4 (1.6) may have chosen other schema names — the prompt says to reuse whatever 1.6 created.
